description:
REQ-013's identity-safety claim is factually false against the ground-truth code it cites, and the gap it leaves is entirely untested by the proof obligations in verification-architecture.md. REQ-013 (behavioral-spec.md:378-391) states: 'THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve every new file this feature reads or writes (the trace corpus read, the override write target) via the EXISTING ANICCA_HOME-gated conventions... explicit ANICCA_HOME env, else $HOME/.anicca, NEVER a shared/ambient path,' and its acceptance criterion claims 'For two distinct ANICCA_HOME values, this feature's write target resolves to two distinct paths... (PROP-017).'

This is true for the WRITE side (instanceOverridePath() in sol-genome.mjs:91-94 is genuinely ANICCA_HOME-gated), but it is FALSE for the READ side -- 'the trace corpus read' this feature is built on. The actual trace file path this feature must read (sol-gate.trace.jsonl, the backtest corpus per REQ-001 and the starvation signal source per REQ-007) is resolved in sol-gate-cli.mjs:37-38 as `STATE_DIR = path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'state')`, `GATE_TRACE_PATH = process.env.SOL_GATE_TRACE_PATH || path.join(STATE_DIR, 'sol-gate.trace.jsonl')` -- i.e. derived from the code's own on-disk location (__dirname), NOT from ANICCA_HOME. If the sol-trade skill code is a single shared checkout (as this repo's own colony architecture implies for shared-code/per-instance-state setups -- CLAUDE.md 'EARN identity解決はANICCA_HOME明示gate必須' memory), this file is a SHARED path regardless of which ANICCA_HOME an instance sets, contradicting REQ-013's blanket claim and the Edge Case 'reads/writes its OWN, separate, empty trace/override files -- never Franklin's' (behavioral-spec.md:386-388) for the read side specifically.

PROP-017 (verification-architecture.md:67) only asserts cross-instance isolation for 'this feature's write target (override path)' -- it explicitly does not cover the trace-corpus READ path at all. This means the starvation signal (REQ-007's countConsecutiveSkips) and the backtest corpus (REQ-001) could, as specified, be computed over a trace stream that is not actually scoped to this instance, with zero proof obligation ever verifying that. REQ-013 must be corrected to either (a) accurately scope its claim to the write path only, or (b) require the trace-read path to also become ANICCA_HOME-gated (a change to sol-gate-cli.mjs's existing GATE_TRACE_PATH resolution, which REQ-013's own text disclaims -- 'no new global/shared state file' does not resolve an EXISTING shared-path read), with a corresponding new PROP added to verification-architecture.md.

evidence.snippet: THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve every new file this feature reads or writes (the trace corpus read, the override write target) via the EXISTING ANICCA_HOME-gated conventions

groundTruthEvidence.snippet: const STATE_DIR = path.join(__dirname, "..", "..", "state"); const GATE_TRACE_PATH = process.env.SOL_GATE_TRACE_PATH || path.join(STATE_DIR, "sol-gate.trace.jsonl");
